rating-ledger-qa.json — one immutable event per rated attempt

competitive_rate_attempt on an already-rated attempt returned {rated:false, reason:'already_rated'} and the ledger stayed at 5 rows. A direct duplicate insert of an existing event was refused by 23505 duplicate key value violates unique constraint "competitive_events_once" (challenge_attempt_id, rating_version) — one attempt id can create at most one immutable event, enforced in storage, not only in application code.
rating-concurrency-qa.json — six simultaneous completions, one event; Postgres: two ordered advisory locks + unique constraint

The event insert and both profile updates happen inside competitive_rate_attempt in one transaction, after pg_advisory_xact_lock on both accounts taken in a fixed order (least, greatest) so two concurrent completions sharing an account cannot deadlock; a caller that waited re-checks the ledger and returns already_rated. The unique constraint competitive_events_once is the storage-level backstop, proven above. Six simultaneous completions producing exactly one event is certified on the harness (rating-concurrency-qa.json).

Both conditions are required, live: with 5 rated matches but only 2 unique opponents A had placed_at null and did not appear publicly; a match against a third opponent (6 matches, 3 opponents) set placed_at and A appeared. B likewise placed only on reaching 5 matches and 3 opponents.

As the service role, past the grants: update competitive_profiles set current_rating = 9999 → P0001 COMPETITIVE_RATING_FORGED; set rated_wins = 99 → P0001 COMPETITIVE_RECORD_FORGED; update a rating event → P0001 RATING_EVENT_IMMUTABLE ('A rating event is never edited.'); delete a rating event → P0001 RATING_EVENT_IMMUTABLE ('A rating event is never deleted; past opponents keep what they earned.').

Unmet: a seeded live challenge code was provided (LIVE_CHALLENGE_CODE); a live expired code was provided (LIVE_EXPIRED_CODE); a live revoked code was provided (LIVE_REVOKED_CODE) — these three need live 9C challenge codes supplied as operator fixtures, and the certified preview database is deliberately empty (Phase 9C's own live rows were deleted when that phase closed), so there is no live row to point them at. Seeding synthetic 9C challenges on the preview the owner is about to test on is outside Phase 9E's scope.
